title: PRUNING x IIT4-Phi — does pruning the WEAKEST edges preserve big-Phi better than random/strongest edges?
verdict_note: DERIVED from measured Phi-retention curves — NOT self-declared. weak-first edge pruning does NOT preserve big-Phi better than random-first pruning: panel-mean retention-AUC weak=0.16224 < random=0.22742, and weak wins the per-substrate head-to-head on only 4/10 (minority). Pre-registered falsifier satisfied on BOTH clauses.
edge_model: ECA neighbour dependency (j->i); prune = force-0 that input bit in the rule-lookup index, KEEP all n nodes; weight = avg output-sensitivity over 2^n global states
falsifier: weak Phi-retention AUC NOT > random AUC across panel (panel-mean OR majority head-to-head) ⇒ H1 FALSIFIED
metric_definition: retention(step k) = bigPhi(pruned_k) / bigPhi(unpruned); AUC = mean retention over all prune fractions (deterministic fn of measured Phis)

panel.note: degenerate: pure-XOR rule, bigPhi=0 at sys=11 (no signal — same as H_312)

finding: H1 PRIMARY FALSIFIED. Selectively pruning the WEAKEST edges does NOT preserve big-Phi better than pruning RANDOM edges: weak loses the panel-mean retention-AUC (0.162 < 0.227) AND wins the per-substrate head-to-head on only 4/10 (minority). Robust to excluding the degenerate eca90 cell (0.180 < 0.253). SECONDARY (not the test target): weak DOES beat strong on panel-mean AUC (0.162 > 0.129) and 5/10 head-to-head — pruning the strongest edges is the worst strategy, which is intuitive, but does not rescue H1. The brain-inspired 'shed weak connections, keep integration' intuition is FALSE on faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi: big-Phi is a non-additive integration measure where even low-sensitivity edges carry distinction/relation structure, so removing them is not Phi-cheap.
secondary_degradation: Across orderings the Phi-vs-fraction curve is CLIFF-like, not graceful: most substrates collapse to retention 0 within the first ~5-7 edges pruned (of 8-12 present), with frequent non-monotone bumps >1.0 (pruning an edge can transiently RAISE big-Phi by removing a partition-favourable connection). No ordering exhibits graceful linear degradation.
